newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan rail crash toll rises to 119.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan rail crash toll rises to 119.

text.p: A runaway train crashed in Pakistan's central province of Punjab on Monday, killing 119 people and injuring 81, hospital officials said.
They said the dead from the crash near the town of Khanewal, 45 km (28 miles) east of the city of Multan, included 70 men, 27 women and 22 children.
The officials said 25 of the 81 injured had been seriously hurt and transferred to Multan. Twenty-five had been discharged and 31 were being treated in Khanewal's Civil Hospital.
Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif arrived in Khanewal by helicopter to inspect the scene of the crash, which occurred at about 4.00 a.m. (2300 GMT Sunday), and offer condolences.

Railway officials said the Karachi-bound passenger train had failed to stop at a junction, apparently because of brake failure. Controllers diverted it on to a dead-end track to prevent a head-on collision with the Lahore-Karachi Shaheen Express train coming the other way on the single main track.
The diverted train then hit the buffers at the end of the spur line near the village of Mirshah, about five km (three miles) from Khanewal, derailing the engine and five coaches.
